milestones.title: First raid with Artimis
milestones.blurb: Mixed-guild Molten Core — the earliest confirmed raid containing Artimis.
milestones.blurbHtml: Mixed-guild Molten Core — the earliest confirmed raid containing Artimis.
milestones.html: The screenshot from 22:09 that night shows a nearly full room gathered before Magmadar, guild tags still mixed — a coalition raid slowly becoming a guild team. Artimis, Dejvid, Divinestorm, Kodf and Jellopy are all in frame: five people whose decisions would shape everything that follows, standing in the same corridor a year before any of it happened.

milestones.title: The hunter diary begins
milestones.blurb: Onyxia and an 8/10 Molten Core clear; Artimis starts organizing the hunters.
milestones.blurbHtml: Onyxia and an 8/10 Molten Core clear; Artimis starts organizing the hunters.
milestones.html: The screenshot trail from this week shows Artimis stepping, almost by accident, into the job that would define his Classic: invited to the officer meeting on the 13th, and within days coordinating the hunter channel, the gear records, the tranquilizing-shot rotation and the signups. He had joined to collect tier pieces. The spreadsheets had other plans.

milestones.title: Ragnaros down, the Choker drops
milestones.blurb: The kill screenshot survives; the neck later fuels the guild's first loot dispute.
milestones.blurbHtml: The kill screenshot survives; the neck later fuels the guild's first loot dispute.
milestones.html:
The Choker of the Fire Lord is one of the rarest drops in Molten Core and best-in-slot for every caster and healer in the raid — which made it a test the young guild's loot rules weren't ready for. The policy gave damage casters priority on the neck, on the argument that gearing damage cleared content faster. To the healers, it read differently: the people who kept everyone alive were structurally second in line for the best item they could ever get.

Nobody said much on the night. The resentment surfaced five weeks later, when Deliz — one of the guild's core healers and part of the Nittedal circle — quit the game entirely, naming the treatment of healers and their exclusion from best-in-slot rolls, with the Ragnaros neck as the concrete example. It was the guild's first fairness crisis, and its shape — effort versus optimisation, the meters versus the people who don't appear on them — returned in every loot fight that followed, from the tank-gear debates of spring to the benches of December.

milestones.title: David hands over the guild
milestones.blurb: Dejvid hands over Discord ownership; Artimis is guild leader in practice.
milestones.blurbHtml: Dejvid hands over Discord ownership; Artimis is guild leader in practice.
milestones.html: David had founded Sleep with a complete joke of a rank ladder — Awake, Light Sleeper, Deep Sleeper, REM Sleeper, Dreamer — and a pitch about a helpful community. By early 2020 he was ready to step back, and the Discord ownership transfer on 1 February made official what the paperwork already showed: Artimis, the hunter officer with the spreadsheets, was running the guild. David's priest Dejvid stayed in the records as the founder; his best-documented later act was having promoted Shakey to priest class leader, a decision Artimis inherited along with everything else.

milestones.title: Deliz quits
milestones.blurb: Criticism of healers and the caster-first Choker policy; he leaves the game the same night.
milestones.blurbHtml: Criticism of healers and the caster-first Choker policy; he leaves the game the same night.
milestones.html: Deliz was Nittedal — one of the real-life friends the guild was built around — and a healer, which made his exit hurt twice. His complaint was structural, not personal: healers were excluded from best-in-slot rolls while damage dealers geared, with the Ragnaros Choker as the standing example. He quit the game the same night he said so. The question he left behind, what a raid owes the people who keep it alive but never top a meter, came back in every fairness crisis the guild ever had — the tank-gear fights of spring, the Rejuvenating Gem, and December's benches.

milestones.title: Blackwing Lair opens
milestones.blurb: Sleep enters on day one.
milestones.blurbHtml: Sleep enters on day one.
milestones.html: Sleep walked in on day one, twelve days into Artimis's formal leadership. The instance became the guild's home for half a year of Sundays — the place where the Dark Iron crafting projects, the gear-weight formulas and the Thunderfury bindings all earned their keep — and the site of its fastest conquest: the whole raid dead within ten days of the doors opening.

milestones.title: Nefarian falls
milestones.blurb: BWL 8/8 within ten days.
milestones.blurbHtml: BWL 8/8 within ten days.
milestones.html: Ten days from the gates opening to the end boss dying — the fastest the guild ever moved through new content, and proof that the friendly community had quietly become a capable raid. The week also produced one of the archive's best recruitment stories: Artimis mailed a cloak to a stranger he had mistaken for someone else, invited him along to BWL anyway, and accidentally acquired Glory, the most loyal tank the guild would ever have.

milestones.title: First Rejuvenating Gem
milestones.blurb: Shakey wins the roll the day Fnats steps back.
milestones.blurbHtml: Shakey wins the roll the day Fnats steps back.
milestones.html: The full story of this night surfaced years later in a private thread. Fnats — druid, ex-mythic raider, one of the guild's two best healers — had spent about two months trying to get the gem's priority settled and eight days waiting for an answer about the healing-officer role, which had been advertised and previously held by Randy. Then Shakey, the priest leader Dejvid had appointed, won the first roll. That same evening Artimis offered Fnats the healing-officer role at last; Fnats took a break from the game instead, for exams and out of patience, with the line every guild leader eventually hears: "as guild leader, you unfortunately stand in the crossfire." His deeper point outlived the night — the people deciding loot for healers were people who would never play one.

milestones.title: Glory's first Binding
milestones.blurb: Both Garr and Baron Geddon die four times that night across split runs.
milestones.blurbHtml: Both Garr and Baron Geddon die four times that night across split runs.
milestones.html: Four Garr and Baron Geddon kills in one night across split runs, and one of them finally dropped a Binding of the Windseeker for Glory. The same date marks the birth of the loot log itself: Artimis started the central spreadsheet that day with a plea that every class leader record every drop. Everything the loot pages on this site know traces back to that decision. The Binding also enrolled Glory in the guild's longest storyline — his Thunderfury completed in November 2020, weeks before December made the legendary feel like a parting gift.

milestones.title: The baby announcement
milestones.blurb: Nefarian dies twice; Anders tells the raid he is expecting a child and promotes Divinestorm on the spot.
milestones.blurbHtml: Nefarian dies twice; Anders tells the raid he is expecting a child and promotes Divinestorm on the spot.
milestones.html: The screenshots catch it all in the same minute: Nefarian dead for the second time that evening, the raid chat filling with congratulations, and the guild-system line recording that Artimis has made Divinestorm the new Guild Master. He told the raid he was going to be a father and gave the guild away in the same breath. Nereb, Pnats, Carmelia, Zados and Luivi answered in kind; Zados thanked the old leader and welcomed the new one in a single message. Nobody in the archive ever managed a cleaner exit.

milestones.title: Sleep + Ninjas become Dusk
milestones.blurb: A new name from a poll, so neither guild absorbs the other.
milestones.blurbHtml: A new name from a poll, so neither guild absorbs the other.
milestones.html: The name came from a poll precisely so that neither guild could claim the other had been swallowed — which is exactly what the Ninjas officers privately believed they were doing. Their channel from the merger weeks calls it "absorbing their guild" outright, and one scout who watched a Sleep raid doubted the merchandise could clear AQ. The Ninjas officers took a formal emoji vote on the 15th; the first raid as Dusk was planned within the week. Sleep's farewell post asked everyone to "make the move over to the Dusk discord with ease" — a server that still exists today under a different name.

milestones.title: First Dusk AQ40
milestones.blurb: The preparation machine: resistance sets, rerolled professions, consumable pipelines.
milestones.blurbHtml: The preparation machine: resistance sets, rerolled professions, consumable pipelines.
milestones.html: The preparation machine behind this night was the merged guild's first real product: nature-resistance sets planned in spreadsheets, professions rerolled on schedule, and a consumables pipeline that would soon be counting venom sacs in the hundreds. Four bosses died on the first evening. C'Thun followed within five days, answering the Ninjas scouts' doubts about "the quality to clear AQ" faster than anyone had a right to expect.

milestones.title: The Ninjas bloc departs
milestones.blurb: Nearly the whole ex-Ninjas core raids its last Dusk night; the merger has failed.
milestones.blurbHtml: Nearly the whole ex-Ninjas core raids its last Dusk night; the merger has failed.
milestones.html: The morning began with Orish quitting live in the officer channel — "Leadership's going to run this guild into the ground, I'm out before it gets much worse" — the second ex-Ninjas officer gone in a week, after Aki's exit over the entrance-pull affair. By afternoon the structure itself had changed: Rockafella said the quiet part ("class leaders think they are officers"), and the officers split the chat in two within the hour. The same day's debate about publishing the officer logs — "we can just let people read the officer chat" against "how do we handle another Nayla situation?" — is the most honest conversation about transparency the guild ever had.

milestones.title: GM crisis
milestones.blurb: Yeat transfers guild master mid-conflict; Divinestorm manages it remotely.
milestones.blurbHtml: Yeat transfers guild master mid-conflict; Divinestorm manages it remotely.
milestones.html: The strangest day in the record: Yeat, holding the in-game guild-master character, kicked Jón Snjór without consulting anyone, tangled in an accusation Divinestorm privately doubted was true. Jón, through his alt's rank, kicked Henne in retaliation; protest gquits followed, including the newly appointed paladin leader. Divinestorm untangled it from a work trip, everyone came back within a day, and kick rights were restricted for good. Henne's terms for returning were the shortest in the archive: "Keep Jon away from me and he can take the drama with him. And I'm good."

milestones.title: Thunderfury
milestones.blurb: Glory's second Binding drops; the legendary is announced the same evening.
milestones.blurbHtml: Glory's second Binding drops; the legendary is announced the same evening.
milestones.html: Glory's second Binding closed a storyline that had run since March, and the guild announced the completed legendary the same evening. It was the raider-rank promise made physical: show up for a hundred raids, do the unglamorous work, and the guild forges you the most famous weapon in the game. Five weeks later the same guild benched him through every Four Horsemen pull. Both things are true, and the distance between them is the whole December story.

milestones.title: Nayla leaves
milestones.blurb: 113 logged sessions; felt unequal to the other tanks.
milestones.blurbHtml: 113 logged sessions; felt unequal to the other tanks.
milestones.html: The exit had three acts: the August discipline case that ended in "one final chance," the September telephone game over his tank spot, and a November departure with a flourish — messages to guildmates about their leader's "last desperate act of evilness," the details of which the archive still doesn't hold. Within two weeks he was raiding elsewhere and loudly himself on the realm Discord. A hundred and thirteen logged sessions deserve the honest summary: he gave the guild enormous amounts of his time, and cost it almost as much.

milestones.title: Dusk enters Naxxramas
milestones.blurb: Three bosses on the first night.
milestones.blurbHtml: Three bosses on the first night.
milestones.html: Noth, Anub'Rekhan and Grand Widow Faerlina fell on Dusk's first night in the citadel — but the run convinced the leadership the guild could not clear Naxxramas alone. The internal review afterwards was blunt, and within forty-eight hours the first conversation with Ascension had happened. The Faerlina kill video is the last recording of Dusk raiding as itself.

milestones.title: Joint raid with Ascension
milestones.blurb: Exactly 20 from each guild, picking the strongest players.
milestones.blurbHtml: Exactly 20 from each guild, picking the strongest players.
milestones.html: Six new bosses died on the first joint evening — Patchwerk, Grobbulus, Gluth, Thaddius, Heigan and Instructor Razuvious — vindicating the partnership overnight and hardening the roster math that had benched twenty people to make it possible. The kill videos from this night carry both guild names in their titles; eleven days later the titles just said Ascension.

milestones.title: Benched — a strike brews
milestones.blurb: Artimis organizes a protest over veterans losing seats; a 37-minute call resolves it the next day.
milestones.blurbHtml: Artimis organizes a protest over veterans losing seats; a 37-minute call resolves it the next day.
milestones.html: The Four Horsemen wall — twelve wipes on the Sunday — sharpened everything: who tanked, who healed, and who watched from outside. On the Monday morning Artimis circulated a five-point proposal demanding raiders before members, whole-lockout spots, and collective bench decisions, while the officers held their own open reckoning about the same grievances in parallel. That evening the Horsemen died on the first pull; neither Artimis nor Glory, the two names at the center of the benching debate, was in the kill — though the private messages show Divinestorm pursuing Artimis all afternoon for a talk ("I know your points"), holding the call at 18:34, and Artimis offering to come once his evening walk ended; the raid filled and killed the Horsemen before he was back. The same night, Divinestorm invited him into the joint officer chat with Ascension. The video is the fight from Anders's own vantage point in a later run.

milestones.title: Kel'Thuzad dies
milestones.blurb: Three wipes, then the last boss of vanilla. 43 names.
milestones.blurbHtml: Three wipes, then the last boss of vanilla. 43 names.
milestones.html: Sapphiron died at 19:53, Kel'Thuzad at 21:23 — Naxxramas cleared fourteen days after the first joint raid, the goal every December sacrifice had been aimed at. The full stream preserves all three attempts and the kill; the short cut is the celebration version. Within days, several of the people who had stayed for the clear left the game, exactly as they had said they would.

milestones.title: Glory's own Kel'Thuzad
milestones.blurb: Left out of the first kill, the guild's most-attended raider gets his — in the archive's final report.
milestones.blurbHtml: Left out of the first kill, the guild's most-attended raider gets his — in the archive's final report.
milestones.html: The last report in the whole archive contains its best ending. Glory — who left Dusk on the night it dissolved, having never been given a Four Horsemen pull — appears in an Ascension-era roster on 11 April 2021, and Kel'Thuzad dies. The guild's most-attended raider got the kill four months late, in the final raid the logs would ever record. History does not usually clean up after itself this well.
